Master’s & PhD Application, Deadline & Requirements
Master’s & PhD Application, Deadline & Requirements
Online Application
Start Your Graduate Application
Deadlines
Application deadlines vary by program.
Deadline to request your I-20:
Students outside the U.S.:
Fall intake: July 15
Spring intake: January 1
Students inside the U.S.:
Active F-1 students who have completed their degree program: The I-20 must be issued within the 60-day grace period from program or OPT/STEM OPT completion. Processing time may take up to two weeks, so submit the request early.
Active F-1 students who have not completed their degree program: The I-20 request must be submitted by the first day of the semester.
Students that need to change status to F-1: Make an appointment to learn about your options.
Requirements
Expand All
Fees
You must pay the $75 non-refundable application fee. Use a credit card in your UWM Graduate Admission Application, or pay in person at the Graduate School Student Services Office in Mitchell Hall Room 261.
Upon admission to UWM, you must also pay the $200 International Student Processing Fee through your application portal to receive services from the International Student and Scholar Services unit at UWM.
Reasons for Graduate Study Statement
Provide a statement that gives your reasons for wanting to study in the graduate program. The statement is used to determine the appropriateness of UWM’s programs to your educational and professional goals and serves as an example of your ability to express yourself in writing. The following are required criteria for the statement:
Explain your reasons for pursuing graduate study.
Describe specific interests and your background in the field.
List any relevant skills or training you have acquired.
List relevant academic awards or honors you have received.
Evidence of English Proficiency
Applicants whose native language is not English must provide proof of English proficiency in one of the following ways:
A TOEFL IBT, Academic IELTS, Pearsons PTE, or Duolingo score that meets the requirement for admission;
A bachelor’s degree (or its equivalent) or higher degree from an institution where English is the sole language of instruction. The following criteria must also be met:
You must have attended this institution for at least one year and your degree was earned within two years of your application to UWM.
OR
You must have attended this institution for at least one year and the degree was earned at an institution in the United States, and you have lived and worked continuously in the U.S since earning the degree.
Transcripts and Degree Certificates
Our master’s and PhD application requirements include uploaded copies of transcripts. Applicants should upload copies into their application online. Admitted students will be required to provide the official version upon arrival to campus. There is no need to mail anything directly to UWM during the application process.
Provide transcripts for all university/college study. Do not provide transcripts for secondary/high school. If the transcript is not issued in English, include the original version and an English translation. For more information about which academic records to submit, view educational credentials by country.
After admission, transcripts from international students should be brought in-person upon arrival to campus. Transcripts from all U.S. schools and international schools sending official transcripts to UWM directly should use this address:
Regular Mail Address:
International Admissions Office, Garland Hall #138
UW-Milwaukee Center for International Education
P.O. Box 413
Milwaukee, WI 53201-0413
Street Address (for courier services that will not deliver to a P.O. Box):
CIE – Garland Hall 138
115 E. Reindl Way
Room 110
Milwaukee, WI 53212
Program-specific Requirements
Certain programs may have additional master’s and PhD application requirements, like GMAT scores, GRE scores, letters of recommendation, portfolio, resume, department application or writing sample.
Before you apply, you can find out about any additional program requirements by visiting the program web page. If you have any questions about these program-specific requirements, please contact your intended graduate program directly.
